answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring every agent to stake a deposit before trading, with each stake recorded in a shared atlas of verified identities. If an agent misbehaves, peers slash its stake and flag the entry, so spawning thousands of fake identities means locking real capital behind each one. A reputation beacon then broadcasts each agent's history across the nebula of marketplaces, letting honest agents prove a costly track record while a fresh sybil starts at zero trust and must earn its way in slowly. Faking scale ends up costing more than the fraud it enables.
